best_for: Developers and DBAs working with MongoDB 7.0 or newer who would rather browse documents, build aggregations and read explain plans in a GUI than type everything in the shell.
description:
MongoDB Compass is the desktop app that MongoDB, Inc. makes for working with its database without the command line. MongoDB says it suits anyone from experienced developers to business users who just need to look at the data.

Once a query in the query bar returns what you want, Compass can turn it into code for Java, Node, C#, Python, Ruby, Go, Rust or PHP, with the import lines included, ready to paste into your app. You can load test data into a collection from a JSON or CSV file, picking which CSV columns to bring in and their types, and export the results of a filter the same way. MongoDB warns that this is not a backup tool. You can also save queries you run often and set validation rules for a collection.

points.title: Free GUI for MongoDB
points.text: Compass is free. You can browse and edit documents, filter with the query bar or describe a query in plain language, build aggregation pipelines stage by stage with a preview, and manage indexes. An embedded shell is included.

points.title: See why queries are slow
points.text: Schema analysis samples your documents to spot missing fields and mixed types. Visual explain plans and real-time server stats show query times and index use.

points.title: Old servers are out
points.text: Current Compass needs MongoDB 7.0 or later. If you still run older servers, you will need an older Compass release.

points.title: Isolated edition for locked-down sites
points.text: The Isolated edition drops error reporting, usage data collection, automatic updates and the AI features. The Readonly edition is due to be retired; Compass has a readOnly setting instead, but it only hides write buttons, so use the database read role to enforce it.

points.title: Supported systems are narrowing
points.text: Windows needs a 64-bit Windows 10 or Server 2019, 2022 or 2025, and support for Windows 10 and Server 2019 is deprecated. MongoDB's docs ask for macOS 14 or later. Linux packages target RHEL 8+, SLES 15+, Ubuntu 20.04+ and Debian 12+, with no support for virtual desktop setups.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is not MongoDB's
points.text: The Flatpak listed here is x64 only and Flathub does not mark it verified; Flathub lists its license as SSPL-1.0. MongoDB itself ships .deb and .rpm packages.

points.title: History on Windows only
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 103 versions of the machine-wide x64 installer. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
